intro_html: Johnny Marzetti is the church-basement casserole that fed half the Midwest for a century, and it still earns its spot: beefy tomato sauce, wide egg noodles, mushrooms, olives, and a melted cheddar lid. Every bowl brings 38 grams of protein for about $4.19 (at everyday cost). Comfort food that respects your budget is rare. This is one of them.
cost_closing_html: About $4.19 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a hearty baked pasta that would run you $13 or more as an entree at a casual Italian place. Make it once and you have two weeks of dinners in the fridge for a fraction of the menu math.
shop_smart: The beef and pork are two thirds of the batch cost. Ground beef in 3 pound packs runs well under the small-tray price per pound, so buy the big pack and freeze what you do not use.
Canned diced tomatoes are one of the most stable prices in the store. Stock up when they dip near 90 cents a can and this casserole gets even cheaper.
Skip the pre-sliced mushrooms. The whole 8 ounce pack is usually the same price or less, and slicing them yourself takes about ninety seconds.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the egg noodles two minutes short of the package time, drain, and set aside. They finish cooking in the oven.
Brown the ground beef and ground pork with the diced onion in your big pot over medium-high heat until no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add the diced bell peppers and sliced mushrooms and cook 5 minutes until they soften.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, brown sugar, dijon, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes so the sauce thickens up.
Fold in the noodles, olives, and half the cheddar until everything is coated.
Spread into a greased 9x13 pan (it will be full) or two smaller pans, top with the rest of the cheddar, and bake at 350 F for about 20 minutes until bubbly and melted.
portion_html: Before it goes in the oven, weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14. That is your per-serving weight. After baking, portion it into 14 containers by that number and every bowl lands at 568 calories and 38 grams of protein.

Brown ground beef and pork with onion, then drain fat.
Cook peppers and mushrooms until soft, then add tomatoes, brown sugar, dijon, and seasonings and simmer 10 minutes.
Fold in noodles, olives, and half the cheddar.
Top with remaining cheddar and bake at 350 F for 20 minutes until bubbly.
